source.title: Permutation Tests for Studying Classifier Performance

confidence_rationale: Supplies the formal framework Q-092's design is an instance of, and adds a distinction Q-092 does not currently make: a label permutation tests whether ANY class structure was found, whereas a restricted within-class FEATURE permutation tests whether the classifier is exploiting feature DEPENDENCY. Q-092's multivariate trajectory-segment signature makes that second test directly applicable and currently unspecified. Foundational, widely-cited, domain-general.
failure_signatures: A label-permutation p-value alone cannot distinguish a classifier exploiting the multivariate DEPENDENCY structure of the trajectory signature from one riding a single dominant marginal feature (e.g. refuge occupancy alone) -- Q-092's Stage-1 claim to a 'multivariate signature' is not established by the test it currently specifies.
Under the label-permutation null the class marginals are preserved, so a strongly imbalanced or degenerate feature set can still yield a misleadingly interpretable result that the null does not flag.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Two complementary permutation tests assess classifier performance: permuting class labels estimates a null for whether the classifier found real class structure; permuting features within classes (a restricted randomisation) estimates a null for whether the classifier exploits dependency between features.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-092 specifies the first test. Its scientific claim, however, is about a MULTIVARIATE trajectory-segment feature signature (refuge occupancy, excursion structure, hazard relationships, transitions, spatial distribution) -- i.e. it wants to claim that behavioural differentiation lives in the joint structure, not in one marginal. Ojala & Garriga's second test is the instrument that separates those, and adding it would let Q-092 distinguish 'reef-ON and reef-OFF differ' from 'reef-ON and reef-OFF differ in the multivariate way the claim asserts'.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a general ML methodology paper with no ecological, behavioural or RL content; it constrains how Q-092 should be ANALYSED and says nothing about whether the reef phenotype exists. It also cannot arbitrate Q-092's matched-control guard, which addresses a confound (environment geometry) rather than a null-hypothesis choice. Adding the feature-permutation test is a refinement to Stage 1, not a substitute for Stage 2's interpretation gate.
mapping.source_context: Machine-learning methodology; synthetic and real datasets including computational-biology applications; classifier-agnostic.

confidence_components.notes: JMLR, heavily cited, classifier-agnostic and domain-general, so transfer risk is minimal. Source quality 0.85 rather than higher only because it is a methods framework whose applicability depends on design choices Q-092 has not yet fixed.
